evidence.quote: Use this page after you open the stage page for the longest stage in a job.
Skew happens when one or a few tasks take much longer than the rest. The other cores sit idle while those tasks finish, which results in poor cluster utilization and longer jobs.

It’s helpful then to inspect the statistics available to Spark and the estimates it makes during query planning and execution.

evidence.quote: When true and spark.sql.adaptive.enabled is true, Spark dynamically handles skew in sort-merge join by splitting (and replicating if needed) skewed partitions.
AQE treats a partition as skewed only when both of these conditions are true: (partition size > skewedPartitionFactor * median partition size) and (partition size > skewedPartitionThresholdInBytes).
AQE also handles skew only in shuffle-based joins, which are sort merge joins and shuffle hash joins. It never optimizes skew in broadcast joins.

statements.note: AQE skew handling applies only to shuffle-based joins, never broadcast joins, and operates on shuffle partitions; the source-partition point is an inference.

edits.rationale: Spark's doc says AQE splits skewed sort-merge join partitions, and Databricks says AQE flags skew only when size thresholds are exceeded and only in shuffle-based joins. It acts on shuffle partitions, so it does not rebalance MongoDB source partitions; that last point follows from these docs rather than being stated outright.
